entry: The Title line under your practice score (Apprenti, Jardinier, Fermier, Maître de Ferme) has gone. Titles now belong to your whole account instead of one game: open your profile page to see your current title and a shelf of every title and what earns it. Your practice score itself is unchanged.

New Exam formats practice, one for each tutorial exercise type that had no practice mode: reading a clock face and writing the time in French, true or false reading, rewriting a sentence (negative or an est-ce que question), answering with a pronoun, reciprocal pronouns and pair questions. Each has its own entry in the practice score. The exam planner also offers the real exam date (Friday 13 November 2026, from the subject outline) with one click.

Week 21 (restaurant and the passé composé) now has seventeen participles of regular verbs, the passé composé tables of regarder, finir and vendre, a rule plot for the negative, a rule plot for object pronouns in the past with the participle agreeing (Sophie l'a écoutée), eight more restaurant words, a short restaurant dialogue and eight past-tense sentences with avoir. 45 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 20 (shops, quantities, the future with aller) now has ten more quantity words (a bar of, a dozen, a hundred grams of, a sachet of), seven quantity sentences, a rule plot for fillings and flavours with à (un sandwich au fromage), ten food-shop and supermarket words, six sentences using y, nine buyer and seller phrases (whose turn is it, that will be all), cheese and fresh produce, and two pronoun plots: object pronouns with the futur proche and en with quantities. 52 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 19 (food and drink) now has about fifty more words: fruit, vegetables, meat, fish and cold meats, sweet things, seasonings and sauces, kinds of milk and breakfast extras, meals and courses (for breakfast, as a starter), and lunch-menu dishes; seven ordering sentences, a rule plot for when the partitive becomes de (not after être), a rule plot for liking verbs (le, la, les) and ten healthy-eating words. 80 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 18 (accessories, weather, object pronouns, vouloir and pouvoir) grew: seasons with au and en, eight weather sentences, more things to pack and four packing sentences, two object-pronoun rule plots (me, te, nous, vous and le, la, l', les), ten verbs that take an object, ten student-life verbs, and as a bonus topic from the Lecture 7 supplement a faire table and a week's weather forecast. 58 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 17 (shopping for clothes) now has six more materials, patterns and styles (plain, short-sleeved, linen, lycra, plastic, imitation leather), a rule plot for the word order noun, colour, material, six opinion words, ten more shop phrases (try on, shoe size, a bit tight, I'll take this one), six ways of asking and giving an opinion, a demonstrative-pronoun-in-use plot (celui de Paul, ceux qui sont en noir) and ten shoe-shop and gift words. 40 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 16 (clothes and colours) now has nine more clothing words (raincoat, stockings, woman's suit, jacket, uniform, tennis shoes, cardigan, tracksuit, to wear), light and dark colours (bleu clair, vert foncé), ten clothes-in-sentences with colour agreement, a colour agreement rule plot with the exceptions (orange, marron, clair, foncé) and six choosing-and-liking phrases. 33 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 15 (months, dates and asking questions) grew: nine question words, dates with the first of the month (le premier), a rule for it, questions asked in other ways (voice, question word last, formal que), how often and how long, eleven words for comparing (in my opinion, cheap, old-fashioned, quiet) and eight comparing and ranking sentences. 41 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 14 (personality, comparing and habits) now has leisure and gym vocabulary: ten faire activities (swimming, DIY, gardening, yoga, skiing), eight jouer phrases that tell games from instruments, gym classes, appointments and parties, seven plan-making sentences, a jouer à / jouer de / faire de rule plot, and the verbs that work like sortir. 47 new plots at the end of the week.

Week 13 (daily routine) now has the reflexive verb tables: wash, get up with its accent change, and get dressed with the shortened pronouns; sentences with parts of the body; eleven more routine verbs (go for a walk, rest, hurry, argue with, get changed); first, then, early, late, during the week; four times a year, at least, almost; a rule for ne ... jamais; talking about days; and seven morning-routine sentences. 48 new plots at the end of the week, nothing you have grown moves.

Week 12 (the FREN152 bridge week) grew to match this year's slides: telling the time minute by minute (quarter past, half past, quarter to, ten to, in the morning or evening), seven example times, asking and saying when something happens, the regular -ir and -re verb lists (think about, pass an exam, visit a person, answer, wait for), a few more -er verbs, and a rule for the plurals in big numbers. 40 new plots, appended to the end of the week, so every plant you already grew stays where it was.

A guide to every colour and icon on the farm. The new Colours and icons panel (the ? button beside the farm, the toolbar, or Menu then Help on the Desktop page) lists each growth stage, mark, border, week-row badge, meter and tag with a small drawn sample next to a plain-words meaning. The samples are drawn the way the farm draws them, so the guide always matches what you see on the plots.

The two semesters now have their own bands on the farm. Semester 1 (FREN151) and Semester 2 (FREN152) each get a heading with the course name, a divider, a progress line and meter of their own, and a Hide weeks / Show weeks button, plus a one-line summary of both above the farm. It is still one continuous farm underneath: the review order, the unlock chain and your save are exactly as before, and which band is folded away is remembered in this browser only. Sorting by weakest, most overdue or type mixes the semesters on purpose, so the bands step aside then and a note says so.

Coins and a Faux Amis game. Every full watering (the first correct answer for a plot each day) now earns one coin, shown under the daily goals; spend coins in the new Farm shop on cosmetic plot skins (terracotta pots, stone tiles, wooden crates, lantern glow, berry hedge, gilded frames). Skins only change how the plots are framed. Faux Amis is a new ten-question game about French words that look like an English word but mean something else (the least look-alike first, the near-twins last). Its list is read live from the French Wiktionary's false-friends page, named on screen with a link, and plots on your farm whose French word is on that list carry a small corner mark and a tooltip saying what it really means. It does not grow plots; your answers count toward the practice score.

Answer checking, round two: typing just the noun is now enough when a question asks for the French word (mode counts for la mode; the article still shows in the feedback), oeuf counts for œuf, spaces around a slash no longer matter, and I'd like counts for I would like. Many English glosses in weeks 6 and 12 to 23 accept the natural alternatives players typed (the road for la rue, is it far/close to here, C'est loin d'ici, it's hot for il fait chaud, to shower, the violin, mineral water, I can / you can / he can). The unreadable-text fix is finished: all 16 combinations of page, visual style and theme were scanned.

Share and tidy-ups: a Copy result button under every finished Review session (your score, plots automated and practice points) and a Share button on each earned achievement. The arcade games now hold their countdowns while this tab is hidden and tell you when you come back (a Settings checkbox turns that off). Answer checking is friendlier to English: commas and hyphens no longer matter, a French accent slipped onto an English word is forgiven, and one-word answers like 'theater' or 'nice' now count when the course glossary allows them. A Credits link sits at the foot of the page and in the Desktop Help menu.

One watering rule everywhere, and more ways to water: the first correct answer for a plot each day, from anything that asks about a real plot (the farm, Review, Quick water, the proficiency tests and every arcade game), waters it fully, and later correct answers for the same plot that day only nudge its next review a day later. A plot you have never watered can now be watered by a game too. A wrong answer in those places changes nothing and a plant never loses a stage. New Water options panel next to Water the next plot, each choice with how many plots it can water right now: a chosen week, a topic (vocabulary, phrases, grammar, pronunciation), the plots wilting most first, 5 quick multiple-choice plots, 5 typed plots, 5 listening plots, or any minigame. Summaries now read 'Plot growth credited: watered 3 plots, nudged 1'.

Four new minigames so every plot has an arcade game: Word Match (pair French and English cards, weeks 12-23), Grammar Gaps (fill the gap in the grammar the other games skip), Listening Pick (hear it, pick what it means) and Word Order Race (put an example sentence's words in order). Every minigame now shows which plot a right answer waters, says what each answer did, and has a Slower, Normal or Faster setting you can change per game (Slower is genuinely relaxed). New plots always start with multiple choice and ask for typed answers more and more as they grow, in the farm, Review and the games; Settings has an Always multiple choice switch and spells out the schedule.

Which activities grow plots: every question screen carries a small text marker saying whether it grows plots and how (with the reason on hover). Proficiency tests and the arcade games credit the plots behind your correct answers through the same rule as watering and Review (see the newer entry below), and each session's summary says what was credited. A game score never grows a plot by itself, and nothing ever goes down.

New on the farm: a golden plot each day (a correct answer on it earns 2 practice points), three small daily goals that earn practice points and leave nothing behind if you skip a day, stubborn weeds (a plot missed four times in a row shows a short re-teach card with the word in syllable pieces and can be rested for a week), a once-per-session slip button that forgives a missed accent or a one-letter typo, session highlights on Review and test results, and a download of your weak items as a CSV or an Anki file from the Progress dashboard.

Readability fixes: the title and other loose text no longer vanish into the pale sky in the dark theme, and dark-on-dark and light-on-light text in the arcade games, Café Rush's second question, the sentence builder tiles, the dashboard and the green buttons was fixed in all four visual styles and both themes, on the Classic and Desktop pages.

Player titles: your practice score now earns a title shown under it, Apprenti, then Jardinier at 25 points, Fermier at 150 and Maître de Ferme at 600, with the next one named. It is worked out from the score you already have, nothing new is saved, and it never changes how plots are scheduled.

Study tools: an Exam planner (enter your exam date and a what-if number of minutes a day to see roughly how much of the farm would be Automated by then, plus the smallest daily effort that reaches 80%), a header countdown chip that only appears once a date is set, a Show and Sort control above the farm (due today, weeds, never watered, by type; weakest or most overdue first), and an accent bar (é è ç œ and more) under every typed-answer box that dims while the accent check is off. None of these changes any plot's schedule (L-9, L-28, L-24, L-20).

Desktop layout: on a wide window with a mouse, the opening screen (and the Menu) now offers a Desktop version of the farm. The whole farm sits in one scrolling stage with your day, plots ready, growth and practice score as chips along the top, the watering and study buttons, the Review tab and the practice games in a column beside it, and every question, test and arcade game opens as a window over the farm that Escape closes. The Classic layout is unchanged, and your save works in both.

Light theme polish for all four looks: the default, low-poly, text-based and cartoon styles each have their own light palette (pale steel and gold, paper with terminal-green ink, cream with violet ink and pink shadows), the farm rows and arcade panels no longer stay dark under the light theme, and small grey captions were darkened to stay readable. Dark mode is unchanged (Y11b).

Story mode: a gentle, optional Story panel follows a small farm at the edge of a village through the seasons, one short chapter for each achievement you earn (plots automated, weeks completed), with the opening chapter there from the start. Chapters only ever appear as you earn them, nothing is shown as missing, and a loaded save brings its chapters back. The shared Story on/off pill hides it, and it never changes a save or how the farm plays (W1).

Placement test: a 🎯 button (and a hint on a brand-new farm) offers an opt-in test that samples the course in six stretches, easiest first, and stops when a stretch gets hard. You then see exactly what would change ("You will start at week N; X plots move to Sprout") and choose Apply or Cancel. Only untouched plots are ever raised, to a modest Sprout with a real due date within a week; nothing already grown is lowered, and answers count toward your practice score (L4b).

Passé Composé Sprint: a fifth arcade minigame, a 60-second, three-lives, combo rapid-fire of fill-in-the-blank and conjugation questions on the passé composé (rows 21-23). It counts toward your practice score like the other four (L1).

Listening practice: a 🎧 button reads a French sentence aloud with your browser's own voices (Play, Slower) and you pick what it means from three English options. It draws on the sentences of every unlocked week and counts toward your practice score (L9).

Conversation simulator: a 💬 button opens a short scripted exchange (meeting someone, getting to know you, asking the way, shopping, a restaurant, time and dates). You pick the French line that fits each turn, from phrases in the course, and a dialogue opens once the weeks it uses are unlocked. Each turn counts toward your practice score (L5).

Sentence builder: a 🧩 button next to Water next opens a freeform builder any time. It shows an English sentence and you tap the French tiles into order, drawing on the sentences of every week you have unlocked. Each finished sentence counts toward your practice score and study days (L11).

Quick water: a 💧 button next to Water next that starts a one-question session on your most overdue plot, for a very short study break. A correct answer waters the plot like any review, and every quick water counts toward your practice score and study days (L29).
New Grammar deep-dive button on grammar questions: the full rule, every example, the look-alikes it is easy to mix up with, and where that plot stands, all in one place.

New Weak-spot drill in the Review tab, built only from what the game has flagged as shaky (known mix-ups first, then your lowest-growth topics). Also, the first correct Review answer for a plot each day now counts as watering it.
New Exam cram in the Review tab: pick a range of weeks and get a dense session of up to 60 items from just those weeks, weakest material first.
New personal phrasebook: star any question while you practise to keep that item in your own list, whatever row it belongs to, and practise just those items on their own.
New Study calendar: a monthly view marking each real day you answered questions, with a small count. It only shows what you did, with no counters to keep alive.
A small gold "Perfect this session" badge now appears on a row once every plot in it has been answered correctly this session, with no misses along the way.
Achievements now show "Earned by N% of players" once enough real save data exists for that achievement (site-wide goal, Z1/Z27b).
Added a keyboard-shortcuts help overlay: press ? to see it, Esc to close it or whichever panel is open (site-wide goal, Z4).
New "My Reports" panel: a small dated feed confirming every correctness or pronunciation report you've sent, from any practice mode (site-wide goal, Z11).
Settings panel: added a "Reset to Default" button that resets the visual style back to High-def in one click (site-wide goal, folded from A26).
New Mixed Review Marathon in the Review tab: a long session of up to 40 due plots from anywhere on the farm, most overdue first.

A batch of small progress and practice details: an opt-in Study buddy that suggests a daily review length, a Farm health section and a scheduling explainer under the Progress dashboard, a plots-automated bar, hover text for row catch-up and automated-plot review countdowns, colour-independent plot borders by topic type, weeds plots that name their look-alike, running accuracy lines for the gender drill and for Sure / Not sure confidence, and a sound legend in liaison practice.

First-run look picker: the first time you open the game on a desktop you can choose High-def, Low-poly, Text-based or Cartoon (or skip for High-def), and change it later in Settings. They are restyles of the same game, not separate artwork.

Practice now counts: the four arcade minigames, the gender drill, liaison practice, proficiency tests and bonus sentences all feed a new Practice score at the top of the farm, with per-mode accuracy on the progress dashboard (capped per day so it can't be farmed, and it never changes your watering schedule).
Row-unlock pacing removed: every week is now open from day one, so joining partway through the real course no longer locks you out of content your classmates already covered.
Visual-style switcher added: choose High-def, Low-poly, Text-based, or Cartoon chrome and palette, changeable any time in Settings.

Pronunciation-risk report button added for known mispronunciation traps; achievements added: two tiers tracking total plots automated and full weeks fully automated; "Weeds" mix-up state, a personal error-pattern digest, a gender-tagging drill, and a liaison/elision practice quiz added; combo bonus, self-rated confidence, deliberate interleaving, adaptive distractor difficulty, a cultural notes toggle, and a progress dashboard added; slideshow cross-check merge: 9 new topics and 75 new items added from the teacher's own lecture slides; core farm launched: the 23-week FREN151 to FREN152 syllabus catalog, spaced-repetition plant growth, a runtime question generator, and save-code support; then grading engine v2 (STRICT/LENIENT tiers), a "flag as correct" report button, a failure feedback blurb, a Review tab, weekly proficiency tests, and bonus sentence-building sections; then site-wide space theme visual pass; also report buttons extended to Review, Proficiency, and Bonus sections, and typed-answer boxes now clear between questions. Also: four arcade minigames added: Greetings & Basics Blitz, Verb Racer, Boutique Dash, and Café Rush — timed, scored alternatives to the calm farm loop, each gated to its own row range. Achievements retrofitted into the hub-wide framework: a static catalog, unlock toast, and hub dashboard link (unlock conditions unchanged).
